text:
maria: quick check — are we aligned on how per-route quotas fall back to global quotas?
I want explicit guidance for 429 responses + headers so SDKs and infra behave consistently.

sahil: short answer: yes, fallback to global is intended when a route has no explicit bucket configured.
But we need to be explicit about headers and the client signals (Retry-After vs bucket id).

lee: agree. main open questions:
1) what headers we return on fallback 429s
2) do we include a per-route bucket id when fallback happens
3) how do we surface whether it was a per-route or global throttle (for metrics/alerts)

jordan: from product POV we want clear signals to users so they can distinguish a route quota vs overall account quota.
Prefer a human-friendly reason in body + machine headers.

emma: SRE note — for rollout, we should avoid changing existing header names. Add new optional headers rather than swapping semantics.
Deprecated behavior will confuse downstream caches and SDKs.

alex: proposal:
- Keep existing headers: `Retry-After`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`
- Add opt-in header `X-RateLimit-Bucket` (string) that contains the bucket id that actually enforced the limit
- Add `X-RateLimit-Fallback: global` when a per-route request was subject to global quota fallback

maria: that sounds reasonable. example 429 response:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 22
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1712345600
X-RateLimit-Bucket: account-global
X-RateLimit-Fallback: global

{ "error": "quota_exceeded", "reason": "route quota not configured, global quota applied" }
```

sahil: two small notes:
- `X-RateLimit-Reset` should be unix epoch secs for clarity
- `X-RateLimit-Bucket` should be predictable (e.g., `route:chat.generate:v1` or `account:global`) so SDKs can parse

lee: agree on format. Also recommend `X-RateLimit-Scope: per-route` or `global` instead of `X-RateLimit-Fallback`? Slight preference for `Scope` for future ext.

jordan: product prefers `X-RateLimit-Scope` — clearer for external customers.

emma: rollout plan suggestion:
1) Add new headers behind feature flag on infra (no semantic change to existing headers)
2) Deploy to canary and monitor 429 rates and SDK parsing errors
3) Announce to customers with example responses and explain backward compatibility
4) After 30d, flip flag for stable traffic

alex: also add integration tests in `infra-rate-limit` that assert header presence for both per-route and fallback cases.
I'll open PR with test vectors.

maria: who can own the docs + SDK updates?

sahil: I'll update the API contract doc and the internal spec (eng-platform). Alex, can you coordinate SDK changes? We should keep server tolerant: if `X-RateLimit-Bucket` missing, SDKs fallback to existing heuristics.

alex: yep. Will add parsing + fallback. Targeting a small patch for all SDKs next week.

jordan: product will draft the external changelog blurb and include migration guidance for customers who parse headers.

deploy-bot: canary deployment started for rate-limiter-v5 on zone-us-east-1 (deployment id: dpl-8821)

emma: monitoring: add alert when `X-RateLimit-Fallback`/`X-RateLimit-Scope: global` exceeds 1% of 429s for first 48h.

maria: sounds good. action items:
- sahil: update internal API contract (due EOD Fri)
- alex: SDK parsing + tests (PR by Tue)
- lee: infra feature flag + canary (inprogress)
- jordan: external docs draft (Weds)
- emma: add temporary alert rule (now)

maria: thanks all — ping me if you need signoff on wording for public docs.

alex: linking draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra-rate-limit/pull/204 — contains test vectors and header parsing examples

sahil: I'll add a section showing example recorded 429s for customers to use in tuning.

maria: cool, will close the loop after canary. :thumbsup:
